syllabus.title: Concepts of Nuclear Physics
syllabus.body: The atom, structure, the nucleus, nuclear structure, atomic transmutation of elements, detection of radio-activity, particle accelerator, decay, natural of elements, nucleus interactions, decay rates, half-life, transuranic elements.

syllabus.title: Neutron Interaction
syllabus.body: Advantages of using neutron, neutron moderation, fission chain reaction, thermalisation of neutrons, fast neutrons, prompt and delayed neutrons, fission products.

syllabus.title: Energy Release
syllabus.body: Mass energy equivalence, mass defect, binding energy, energy release in fission & fusion, thermonuclear reaction, fusion bomb.

syllabus.title: Reactor Materials
syllabus.body: Fissile & fertile materials, cladding & shielding materials, moderators, coolants.

syllabus.title: Reactor Technology
syllabus.body: Basic principles, fuel assembly, neutron balance, reactor kinetics, reactor coefficients, reactor stability, excess reactivity, Xenon poisoning, burnable absorbers, reactivity control, heat balance, production & transfer of heat to the coolant, structural considerations.

syllabus.title: Nuclear Reactors
syllabus.body: Types of nuclear reactors, pressurized water reactors, boiling water reactors, CANDU type reactors, gas cooled & liquid metal cooled reactors, fast breeder reactors.

syllabus.title: Safety Considerations & Waste Disposal
syllabus.body: Hazards, plant site selection, safety measures incorporated in plant design, accident control, disposal of nuclear waste.

syllabus.title: Health Physics & Radio-isotopes
syllabus.body: Radiation: units, hazards, prevention, preparation of radio-isotopes & their use in medicine, agriculture & industry.

outcomes: To understand the concepts of neutron physics and various nuclear Processes involved in Nuclear Power Plants.
To calculate heat generation from nuclear reaction.
To design and analyze the performance of nuclear power plants.
To get acquainted with applications of radioactivity.
To appreciate the hazards associated with radioactivity and the necessity of waste disposal.
textbooks: M. M. El-Wakel, Nuclear Power Engineering, McGraw Hill
Shultis and Faw, Fundamentals of Nuclear Science and Engineering, CRC Press
Stephenson, Introduction to Nuclear Engineering, McGraw Hill
